fixed.summary: Moves frames; re-cooks everything (cooker r16): the base colour texture of a glTF material that tests its alpha (`alphaMode` `MASK`, or a `type model`'s `alphaTest`) gets mips that keep its coverage. Each level is the one before sampled bilinearly at the texel centre (a 2×2 box on even sizes, the two centre taps on odd ones, clamped at the edges: WebGL's `generateMipmap`), and a level that keeps fewer texels at or above the material's `alphaCutoff` than the first level does has its alpha raised until it keeps as many. basisu's own filter spread a leaf card's alpha over the transparent texels around it, so its minified levels fell under the cut-off and the card thinned out and vanished with distance (a 1024×384 bamboo spray had no texel left from its 4×1 level down). The cut-off is taken in the texture's alpha, as the renderer tests it times the material's `baseColorFactor` alpha: 255 × `alphaCutoff` / that factor, rounded up. A material with no such byte keeps the encoder's mips: a cut-off of 0 or less, a factor under the cut-off, or a mesh drawn with it whose vertex colour (`COLOR_0`) alpha falls under 1 somewhere, so materials whose vertex alpha varies keep today's mips. Every other texture keeps the same levels. One image under an alpha-tested and another material, or under two whose cut-offs come to different bytes, now cooks as that many textures.
